declarations.description:
<pp-attract>: a short demo of the markup inside it, played by a pixel pointer from a script, looping while it is
on screen. Its markup is inert and the element is one image to assistive technology, named by label; between loops
every change the demo caused is undone. With less motion asked for, on the device or on the page, it shows its
still frame at once, and plays on when that is lifted. Show it only on a page that shows <pp-motion-toggle>.
declarations.name: PixelAttract

members.name: pointer
members.description: The pointer attribute: "glove", or null for the arrow.

members.name: steps
members.description:
The steps it plays: the ones set here, else the script's. Setting them plays them from the top; null goes back
to the script.

attributes.name: script
attributes.description: The steps, split by ";": move <selector>, press <selector>, type <selector> '<text>', wait <time>, show <selector>, hide <selector>, and poster (the still frame).

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: The one sentence assistive technology reads for the demo: what it shows happening.

attributes.name: pointer
attributes.description: The pointer: the arrow, or the white glove (game screens, touch).

declarations.summary: Attract mode: a short demo of the markup inside it, a pixel pointer pressing its real controls, looping.

declarations.name: burst
declarations.description: Pops sprites out of target. Resolves when the last has gone.

<pp-motion-toggle>: a page-wide pause for motion. It wraps a real button (its own, or the one it makes: a soft
button with a pause icon and its label) whose aria-pressed says whether data-pp-motion="reduce" is on <html>.
Pressing it sets or clears the attribute and remembers the choice on this device; every toggle on the page follows
the attribute, whoever sets it. Show it on every page whose world drifts, flares or has events.
declarations.name: PixelMotionToggle

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: The label of the button it makes when it holds no button of its own.

declarations.summary: A page-wide pause for motion: a button that sets data-pp-motion="reduce" on <html>, and remembers it.

declarations.description:
<pp-drop-text class="pp-display pp-pop" data-pop="Blip">Blip</pp-drop-text>: the letters drop in when
it connects, when its text changes, and on play(). With data-pop, each letter keeps the POP tint.
declarations.name: PixelDropText

members.name: play
members.description: Drops the letters in again. Words stay whole when the line wraps.

attributes.description: With .pp-pop: each letter keeps the POP outline and drop (the element keeps the value in step with the text).
attributes.name: data-pop

attributes.description: With .pp-display: Pixel Bop at this whole scale.
attributes.name: data-scale

attributes.description: With .pp-pop: the tint and the drop's colour.
attributes.name: data-tone

declarations.summary: A Pixel Bop heading whose letters drop in one after another.

declarations.description:
<pp-typewriter mood="happy" blips>Hello there!</pp-typewriter>: types when it connects, when its text changes,
and on play(); finish() shows it all. Fires pp-typewriter-done when the last letter is in. The untyped rest keeps
its room, so nothing moves while it types.
declarations.name: PixelTypewriter

cssProperties.description: The hold after a full stop that ends a word.
cssProperties.name: --pp-duration-stop

cssProperties.description: The hold after a comma that ends a word.
cssProperties.name: --pp-duration-comma

members.name: play
members.description: Types the text from the start.

members.name: finish
members.description: Shows the whole text at once.

events.description: Once per play: when the last letter is in, or on finish().
events.name: pp-typewriter-done

attributes.description: Voices every other letter with the chip blip (through services.sound()). "false" is off.
attributes.name: blips

attributes.description: A two-pixel block after the typed text: still while it types, then it blinks for six beats once the last letter is in, and stays. "false" is off.
attributes.name: caret

attributes.description: With .pp-display: Pixel Bop at this whole scale.
attributes.name: data-scale

declarations.summary: Text that types itself in, a letter at a time.

declarations.name: transition
declarations.description: Runs update behind a transition. Resolves when the new screen is fully shown; rejects if update throws.

declarations.name: worldPalette
declarations.description: The world's colours for a time of day, from the --pp-world-* tokens at an element.

declarations.name: drawWorld
declarations.description:
Draws the world (all five layers, or one) into a 2D context at (0, 0), w x h world pixels: 320 x 180 is the TV's
picture. Scale the canvas up by whole numbers with `image-rendering: pixelated`.

<pp-world>: the world as a backdrop filling its positioned container. Each world pixel is the page's pixel
(--pp-pixel) times `zoom`, made a whole number of device pixels; the canvas is drawn at the world's own resolution
and scaled up crisply, and only redrawn when its size, its screen or its time of day changes.

Attributes: scheme (day, sunset, night, auto, or left out to follow the page), parallax, clouds (drift; "none"
for none), stars (stars flare at night), events (birds by day, a shooting star at night), zoom, avoid (a selector
list of what the sun, the moon, the stars, the clouds and shooting stars keep clear of).

Its motion pauses at once while the person asks for less, on their device or on the page (data-pp-motion="reduce"
on <html>, which <pp-motion-toggle> sets), and carries on from there when they no longer do.
declarations.name: PixelWorld

members.name: avoid
members.description: The avoid attribute: a selector list, or null.

members.name: scheme
members.description: The scheme attribute: day, sunset, night, auto, or inherit (the page's).

attributes.name: scheme
attributes.description: The time of day; "auto" follows the clock. Left out, the page's scheme.

attributes.name: parallax
attributes.description: The layers slide against the pointer, a whole pixel at a time, and lift a little as the world scrolls past. "false" is off.

attributes.name: clouds
attributes.description: Present (or "drift"): the clouds drift, a whole pixel at a time. "none": no clouds. Left out (or "false"): still clouds.

attributes.name: stars
attributes.description: Stars flare now and then at night. "false" is off.

attributes.name: events
attributes.description: Now and then a flock of birds by day, a shooting star at night. "false" is off.

attributes.name: zoom
attributes.description: Page pixels per world pixel, a whole number.

attributes.name: avoid
attributes.description: A selector list of things the sky keeps clear of (".pp-hero-title, .pp-hero-lead"), matched in the world's container (its parent, or the nearest ancestor that holds a match). The sun, the moon and shooting stars go where they cross none of those boxes: the nearest clear place in their lane of the sky, else the same place across the sky if that is clear, else out of sight. Stars and clouds that would sit behind them are left out. Whole pixels, the same every time, and looked at again when anything resizes.

declarations.summary: The dithered world backdrop: sky, mountains, hills and meadow, for Day, Sunset and Night.
